plan: [My private signal s=39. The common value C is uniform 20–29 and all corresponding noises are possible, so the posterior expected common value is E[C|s]=average(20..29)=24.5. In a second-price auction with a common value, bidding your posterior expected common value avoids the winner’s curse and maximizes expected profit. With no prior rounds to learn from, I will bid 24.5.]

[My signal 38 yields a uniform posterior over common value v in [20,29] because noise is uniform; so E[v|s=38] = (20+29)/2 = 24.5. In a second-price auction, bidding my best estimate of the common value avoids the winner's curse and maximizes expected surplus given no history. Therefore bid my conditional expected true value.]

[My signal is 20; unconditional expected common value is 24.5. Because this is a common-value, second-price auction, the winner’s curse makes the conditional value given winning lower than 24.5. To maximize long-run profit and avoid overpaying, I will bid conservatively and not exceed my perceived value. I choose a safe bid equal to my private signal ($20), which limits downside while allowing wins when others bid very low.]
